transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey folks- thanks for making time. We're on for 30 minutes but we can take 40 if needed. I'm Jordan, AE for Redwood Inference. With me is Priya, our SE.
[00:12] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi, everyone. Quick agenda: align on what you want to prove in the POC, the workloads, benchmark plan, and then commercial guardrails - credits, pilot length, and path to procurement.
[00:22] Maya (CTO): Thanks. I'm Maya, CTO. Alan will talk more about the models, and Samir is our infra lead.
[00:27] Alan (Head of AI): Yep, hi. Our main thing is a clinical summarization flow - ingesting visit notes, run an LLM to extract structured findings, then a short-form patient summary. Latency matters for the clinician UI.
[00:39] Samir (Infra): Hey - from infra side we need to know expected RPS and sequence lengths so we can size the environment - also security questions later.
[00:48] Jordan: Great. Can you give us current numbers? QPS, typical input length, and what SLA you need?
[00:54] Alan: Roughly 25 concurrent users, peaky to 60 rps during clinic hours. Typical document length is 500-1,200 tokens, but we also have a long-note batch job that goes to 4k tokens. For the UI path we'd like p95 latency under 800ms ideally.
[01:12] Priya: Okay that helps. For benchmarks we'll separate two workloads: interactive summarization (low latency, shorter seqs) and batch long-note processing (throughput-focused). Do you have targets for quality metrics? Rouge or clinical concordance?
[01:26] Alan: Clinicians care about accuracy of extracted fields - we can provide a set of 200 annotated examples. The success criteria we'd use: 90%+ field extraction accuracy on the sample set, and cost per summary under $0.10 - roughly what finance is expecting.
[01:40] Jordan: Helpful - we'll put those numbers in the plan. On the commercial side, typical Redwood pilot options are 30-90 days with a pilot credit bucket. For your size we usually offer a credits package and a lightweight MSA amendment for pilot terms.
[01:55] Maya: Can you be specific on credits? We need to present this to procurement.
[02:00] Jordan: Sure. For a 60-day pilot we can offer $15k in credits which roughly covers about 1M tokens on our verified models, with on-demand burst into Dedicated if needed. We can also structure the pilot as reserved throughput for a couple hours/day if you want stable latency.
[02:18] Samir: Is that credits or committed spend? Also, what are the upgrade paths if we need Dedicated for SLAs?
[02:24] Jordan: Credits are pre-paid usage credits applied to the hosted account; they don't obligate you beyond the pilot. If you want Dedicated, that's a separate reserved capacity contract - usually a monthly commit. We can map pilot hit rates to a recommended Dedicated configuration and provide a cost comparison.
[02:39] Priya: On benchmarking we recommend baseline runs on your sample data to measure p50/p95 latency and token throughput. We'll run two passes: an initial lightweight run on hosted, then an optimized run with batching, KV-cache warmup, and quantization profiles. We'll also record token-cost per request.
[02:56] Alan: Sounds good. How intrusive is the instrumentation? We prefer using our staging with a short proxy to send requests, not share PHI.
[03:04] Priya: Totally - we can do self-hosted runners or you can run the workload in your VPC if you go Private. For the initial pilot, many customers use hosted with a small sampled dataset that is de-identified. We also support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with KMS integrations for extra protection.
[03:20] Maya: Procurement will want SOC 2 and an audit trail. Do you have the docs to share?
[03:24] Jordan: Yes, we'll attach the security pack - SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML details, and our data retention options. I'll include that in the email with the pilot terms.
[03:34] Samir: Okay good. On throughput: when you say burst into Dedicated, what happens to data isolation? We need guaranteed isolation for PHI in some runs.
[03:42] Jordan: If PHI is required then Dedicated or Private is the recommended path - Dedicated gives you tenant isolation on GPU pools; Private gives full VPC/on-prem options. For the hosted pilot we'd plan to use de-identified data. We'll call out the transition criteria in the pilot doc.
[03:57] Priya: Quick note on measurement - to pick a Dedicated config we need distribution of sequence lengths and concurrency over a typical clinic day. Samir, can you share a sample hour of traces?
[04:06] Samir: Yes, I'll extract a day from our staging logs and send it. Expect CSV with timestamp, seq_len, request_type.
[04:13] Alan: On success criteria beyond accuracy and cost, we want stability - no more than 1 outage or degradation during a 30-day window, and graceful fallback if Redwood is unavailable.
[04:23] Jordan: We can include fallback guidance in the POC runbook - model variant fallbacks and retries. Also will set up alerting hooks to your SRE.
[04:30] Maya: Timeline - we'd like to kick off baseline within two weeks. Procurement may take 3-4 weeks after pilot if the metrics are good.
[04:38] Jordan: So tentative schedule: share terms and security docs by 2025-10-09; benchmark plan and workload script by 2025-10-10; you provide datasets by 2025-10-13; baseline run week of 2025-10-20. Does that align?
[04:49] Maya: Yes.
[04:51] Priya: On the technical side we also need to define the benchmarks: p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, field extraction accuracy, and memory usage for long sequences. We'll measure both single-request latency and batch throughput with continuous batching enabled.
[05:06] Alan: For models, we're testing a mixture - a compact open model for cost and a larger verified model for quality. Will Redwood support both?
[05:12] Priya: Absolutely - we'll map them in the model catalog and run side-by-side comparisons. Note: optimization paths (quantization, kernel selection) may change latency numbers, we'll call out what optimizations were enabled in each run.
[05:24] Jordan: Quick commercial guardrail notes: the pilot credits cover hosted usage only; Dedicated evaluation requires a separate sizing exercise and quote. If procurement needs a PO, we can accept one against the credits; otherwise, we can do a short MSA amendment for pilot terms.
[05:38] Maya: If we hit the success criteria early, what's the contracting path? Fast-track to a committed Dedicated contract?
[05:44] Jordan: Yes - we usually create a procurement path doc - options: 1) convert remaining credits into committed spend with a discount; 2) sign a Dedicated monthly commit with onboarding SLA; 3) go Private with enterprise licensing. We'll include ballpark numbers so procurement can evaluate.
[05:58] Samir: Anything in the pilot that would lock us into a long term license? We need flexibility to move off in-house if things change.
[06:05] Jordan: No lock-in - credits are one-off. Dedicated and Private are separate contracts; we can structure a pilot-to-production transition that suits you.
[06:12] Alan: One risk: accuracy drift over time - do you support continuous evals and data ops to detect regressions?
[06:18] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals. For the pilot we'll set up a small eval set and weekly checks.
[06:28] Maya: Okay, can you email the pilot one-pager now?
[06:31] Jordan: We'll follow up right after this call.
[06:33] Alan: A couple of smaller items - encryption at rest, audit logs, and RBAC for teams. We need examples of your audit trail records format.
[06:41] Jordan: Included in the security pack - audit logs and RBAC screenshots.
[06:45] Samir: I'll add our security checklist items to the shared doc.
[06:48] Priya: Final note on benchmarks - please include the long-note batch workload with 4k tokens and measure out-of-memory events; we'll attempt a quantized run to see memory improvements.
[06:58] Jordan: Great. To recap: deliverables from Redwood: pilot credits/pricing + security docs (Jordan), benchmark plan & workload scripts (Priya). Deliverables from Saffron: sample datasets, seq-length distribution, and decision timeline from procurement.
[07:14] Maya: That works. Thanks everyone.
[07:17] Jordan: Thanks - we'll send the follow-up and get the pilot doc out today.
[07:21] Speaker 1: meeting ended
